newsitem.title: GERMANY: PORSCHE MAY MAKE SPORT UTILITY CAR ALONE.
newsitem.headline: PORSCHE MAY MAKE SPORT UTILITY CAR ALONE.

text.p: Sportscar maker Dr.Ing.h.c.F. Porsche AG is willing to develop a sport utility vehicle by itself after efforts to find a partner have fallen through, chairman Wendelin Wiedeking told a German newspaper on Thursday.
Wiedeking told the Handelsblatt newspaper that improved economic conditions made it possible for the company to produce such a vehicle assuming certain preconditions were met.
Porsche had previously said it was in talks with fellow German car maker Mercedes-Benz to jointly produce a sport utility vehicle in the U.S. modelled on Mercedes M-Class.
But the talks collapsed in January because of concerns at Mercedes that the car would not be profitable enough.
Wiedeking said production of a sport utility car would give the company's sales a new dimension, making it less dependent on what can be a fickle sports car market.
Porsche currently makes only two models, the 911 and the recently introduced Boxster.
